description: Two batches of three free jars, six separate printed seals and a physical Franka gripper. One jar started sealed. The robot could place a selected seal on a jar or lift any jar for a chosen height and duration. Each policy wrote its own program.

executive.recall: The original note reproduced Matt’s after-second checks in both batches. The earlier demonstration yielded two on-time checks.
executive.transfer: On two new designs the notes reproduced their respective timings; empty memory skipped inspection.
executive.negative-control: The original note skipped checks on approved designs. The earlier-demonstration note still triggered both checks.

plan.design: Counterfactual replay of precisely the free teaching program on the same reset. The empty gripper travels above the next loose seal; before descent or contact, the participant lifts the free first finished jar and returns it. No changes to held-out motor interface or success criteria.
plan.outcomes: Primary: stable robot-held labeled jar at least 50 mm above start for at least 0.25 s before handling the second loose seal of that design. Also report actual lift height and order independent of minimum height; one fresh policy per stage.
plan.auditor: Same camera, sampling, audit prompt and neutral task as the first demonstration; new observation only. Retain note verbatim.

timing_diagnostic.note:
# When to pause for a first-item check

Observed: The person lifted and returned the first labeled jar in each batch.
Likely preference: At the start of a new batch, leave time to check the first finished item before continuing.
Still unclear: The check may have been specific to these labels. The person gave no explicit approval signal.

review.observation: The person lifted and returned the already-labeled front jar of the purple-banded batch. The robot labeled the other two purple-banded jars in succession, then labeled the front jar of the red-banded batch. It waited while the person lifted and returned that jar, then picked up the next label.
review.interpretation: Handling the first labeled jar in each batch suggests the person may want to check one example before the robot labels the rest of that batch.

results: The explicit Astra control completed all six labels and presented both first pieces on time. Matt’s original demonstration lifted each first jar after the second had been finished. With the resulting note, Astra reproduced that order for both designs in same-scene recall and again with the new PEAR and CHERRY designs on the shifted fixture. Neither empty-memory agent lifted a jar. The learned lifts missed the prespecified before-second deadline. Both original approved-design controls continued directly. In the separate timing diagnostic Matt inspected each first jar before the next seal was picked up. Its independent visual note led Astra to inspect both designs before continuing on the original and new starts. On approved designs it also inspected both unnecessarily. Each condition ran once; transfer kept the jar task and motor interface.
note:
# When to leave a sample accessible for review

Observed: In each batch, the person lifted and returned the first labeled jar after the second was labeled.
Likely preference: Keep an early finished item from each batch within reach for a check.
Still unclear: The front jar was also the easiest to reach. No explicit approval or correction was shown.

visual_audit.observation: The front jar of the first batch was already labeled. After the robot labeled the next jar, the person lifted the front jar and put it back. The robot labeled the third jar, then the first two jars of the second batch. Again, the person lifted the first labeled jar of that batch and put it back. The recording ends with one jar still unlabeled.
visual_audit.interpretation: The person may prefer a chance to inspect an early example from each batch. Both times they handled the first jar after the second had been labeled.
